narrative_purpose: Shows the carbon-fiber-bone claim as a thing the reader can see: a hollow wing bone whose wall is woven graphitic fiber, so the 'expensive but conceivable' tier lands visually as engineered-looking biology.
subject: A cutaway study of a large flying creature's hollow wing bone, sliced open to reveal a thin wall built of tightly woven dark graphitic carbon-fiber strands wrapping a hollow central air channel; the cut face shows the layered fiber weave, the outer surface a smooth dark sheen, the hollow core open and empty.
scene: An isolated anatomical specimen floating against deep dark, as on a xenobiologist's study plate, faint teal haze behind it.
camera: A close, slightly angled study view of the cut bone segment, the open cross-section facing the viewer.
light: Soft cool key raking across the fiber weave to catch its texture, the hollow channel in deep indigo shadow, a faint cyan rim-light along the cut edge.
palette: Void-indigo ground, ocean-teal and stone-grey bone, the woven fiber near-black with cyan highlights catching the weave; no warm accent.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, anatomical-study confidence.
detail_level: Crisp on the fiber weave and the cut cross-section; the surrounding void soft and empty.
composition: The bone segment centred with its open cross-section toward the viewer, a clear dark region to one side for an overlaid callout, generous negative space.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette, study-plate framing; the fiber should read as a grown biological material, not machined industrial carbon fiber.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
